## Summary
Adds a new full-width **Pokédex** view, toggled from the header (`Calculator | Pokédex`), that lists every Pokémon for the selected regulation in a Pokémon Showdown teambuilder–style table: small sprite, type(s), abilities, HP/Atk/Def/SpA/SpD/Spe and BST.

Two interactions, as requested:
1. **Search** — filters by name **or** ability.
2. **Sort by stat** — clicking a stat header sorts high→low; clicking again sorts low→high (with a ▲/▼ indicator). Name and BST are sortable too.

## How it works
- **Regulation M-A**: eager-loads the whole roster with a live progress count, reusing the localStorage-cached `fetchPokemonDetails`. The roster is the base species from `champions_dex.json` **plus their Mega and regional variants** (`-mega`, `-alola/-galar/-hisui/-paldea`) pulled from the full PokéAPI variety list; cosmetic/gimmick forms (gmax/totem/cap/…) are excluded.
- **None (National Dex, ~1500)**: rows render name-first and lazy-load stats on scroll via `IntersectionObserver`; the first stat-sort or ability-search triggers a one-time full load.
- Base species whose default form carries a suffix not in `champions_dex.json` (`aegislash`→`aegislash-shield`, `mr.rime`→`mr-rime`, etc.) are resolved via the species endpoint and cached under the original slug.

- `src/data/dex.js` (new) — pure `bst` / `sortDex` / `filterDex` logic, unit-tested.
- `index.html` — header toggle + `#page-pokedex` table markup.

body:
## Summary

- On Windows, `tokio::time::Instant` is anchored at system boot, so within the first 60s of uptime the rate limiter's `now - window` (window = 60s) underflows and std panics with *"overflow when subtracting duration from instant"*. This reliably fires on **autostart** (the daemon launches seconds after boot) but never on manual launch — which is exactly the pattern seen in the field. Fixed by using `checked_sub` in both `check` and `cleanup_stale`; when it underflows no entry can be stale yet, so pruning is skipped (832b62c9).
- The periodic cleanup task hit this immediately because `tokio::time::interval` fires its first tick right away, so `cleanup_stale` ran `now - window` at daemon startup.
- Added two deterministic regression tests that force the underflow via an oversized window (no dependency on real uptime).

Resolves Sentry issues **UNICLIPBOARD-RUST-1B** and **UNICLIPBOARD-RUST-1Y**.

🚨 **Severity**: CRITICAL

💡 **Vulnerability**: Two instances of XSS were identified in `src/app/api/auth/magic/callback/route.ts`:
1. Use of `innerHTML` to render text messages, creating a DOM-based XSS vector.
2. Unescaped usage of `JSON.stringify(email)` and `JSON.stringify(token)` inside an inline `<script>` tag. An attacker could supply an email containing `</script><script>alert(1)</script>` to terminate the script block early and execute arbitrary JavaScript.

🎯 **Impact**: An attacker could craft a malicious magic link that executes arbitrary JavaScript in the victim's browser, potentially stealing session tokens or manipulating the StealthRelay dashboard.

🔧 **Fix**:
- Switched `div.innerHTML` to `div.textContent` in the `addLog` UI handler.
- Appended `.replace(/</g, '\\u003c').replace(/>/g, '\\u003e')` to the `JSON.stringify()` interpolations inside the script block to escape HTML angle brackets, neutralizing script breakout payloads.

✅ **Verification**: 
- Code review performed to verify `textContent` and unicode escaping is functioning.
- Build successfully verified via `pnpm run build`.
- Tests successfully verified via `pnpm test` and `npx playwright test`.

body:
## Bug (found by the Phase 6 wrap-up audit)

The transaction player-chain link columns (added/dropped × next/prev, from #184) were populated with **garbage on every row that has no added (or no dropped) player**.

Root cause: pure-drop rows carry `Player Added` as **NaN/None** in memory (it's only rendered `"N/A"` at write time). `str(NaN)` → `"nan"`, which is truthy and `!= "N/A"`, so it slipped past the guard. Every no-add row collapsed into a single phantom `chains["nan"]` bucket and linked to the previous/next *other no-add transaction* — **362 rows** on the added side, symmetric on the dropped side.

## Fix
A `_real_player()` helper that rejects blanks and the `nan`/`none`/`n/a`/`0.0` sentinels, used in both the chain build and the fill loop (and reused by `_is_player_asset`, which previously filtered `None`/`N/A` but not `nan`).

## Verification (simulated on the current build)
- No-add rows: added-link populated **361 → 0**.
- Real-add rows: chains **unchanged** (829 still linked; Ronald Jones 2021-12-01 added-next still → `#16`).
- Symmetric fix on the dropped side (no-drop rows).

## Phase 6 wrap-up status
This was the **only** issue the holistic audit surfaced. Everything else passed: schema matches catalog (43/28 cols), FAAB premium % ∈ [0,100], Player addition value 0 blank, #picked-up/#dropped correctly gated, KTC dates exact, tanking delta both-signed, all link refs in range. - New Layout module: virtual canvas is now 1280×720, with the battlefield kept at a fixed world size and centered/letterboxed via a world viewport (game logic and coordinates unchanged).
- Mouse mapping and SetGameScissor are world-aware.
- Dark frame around the game canvas so all field/border intersections are visible.

### HUD reframe

- Full-height left command column consolidates stats, controls, the wave panel, and the inspect view; compact top strip for toggles (auto-fire / damage numbers / auto-wave) and speed (>, >>, >>>); roll/purchase buttons in the bottom tray.
- Stored turret cards live in the bottom tray; redesigned borderless toggles and card-style action buttons.

### Incoming-wave panel (formerly "Hoard" → "Horde")

- Renamed header to "INCOMING — WAVE X", always showing the wave number (planning and in-progress).
- Stays live during a wave: enemy counts drain as they're killed, cleared types dim out, and an "in progress…" tag shows while active. Red spawn-direction arrows mark where the wave enters from.

### Inspect / Base Journal

- Inspect card previews hovered/selected turrets (upgrade- and buff-aware) and enemies; sticky click-to-pin focus. Hover info cards for locked (token) and empty build slots (no rarity).
- Base Journal: enemy/turret encyclopedia with discovery tracking, opened from a wide button at the bottom of the column.

### Menus & cursors

- 16:9 resolution/settings menu (fullscreen/windowed, stacked resolutions, audio), reused as the in-game pause panel; added a Quit Game button.
- Custom cursors: OS hand/arrow over UI (matching the menu), red aim dot only over the battlefield; normal pointer over the base build area.

### Gameplay & fixes
- Right-click to pick up a placed building back into the deck.
- Base now renders a single green wall on the enemy-facing side.
- Misc fixes: duplicate "press enter to start" prompt, duplicate unlock-slot tooltip, token singular/plural text, card title/description overlap; hook stun duration and Duplicator health tuning; child-bullet hit-cache deep copy.

Adds a real **iOS app target** (iOS 26) to the previously macOS-only app, sharing the existing SwiftUI sources, and wires up **on-device Apple Intelligence** as the default backend stack on iOS.

This PR touches `TranscriptionCore`, `TranscriptionApp`, the Xcode project, CI, and docs — calling that out per the contributing guidelines.

author: mynock
body:
## Why

The invoice matcher only considered work activities with `status = 'completed'`. But Notion-synced activities are imported as **`needs_review`** and stay there until approved — so they were invisible to the matcher, and their invoice lines all came back **`unmatched`**.

## What

Widen the candidate query from a single status to:

```ts
const MATCHABLE_ACTIVITY_STATUSES = ['completed', 'needs_review'];
```

Both represent **work that actually happened**. Deliberately still excludes:
- `invoiced` — already billed; must not re-match
- `planned` / `in_progress` — not done; billing those (and flipping them to `invoiced` on a match) would be wrong

One-line change to the `runMatcher` candidate query (used by both initial sync and rematch), plus the named constant + a comment explaining the choice.

## Behaviour note

A `needs_review` activity that auto-matches now flips to `invoiced` — i.e. matching it to an invoice effectively bypasses the manual review step. On a later unmatch, `revertOrphanedActivities` returns it to `completed` (not back to `needs_review`). Both are reasonable, but flagging them since they're subtle.

## Testing
- Server `tsc` clean; 23 `invoiceImportService` unit tests pass.
- The candidate query lives in `runMatcher`, which has no DB-backed integration test (existing orchestration-coverage gap) — verify via a dry-run **Preview sync** that previously-unmatched invoices now match.

> After this lands: re-run a dry-run sync (or per-invoice rematch) on a client whose work was stuck in `needs_review` and confirm the lines now match.

## Summary

This PR implements four critical backend features for HubAssist: Cloudinary asset cleanup, dashboard response caching, CSRF protection, and full-text user search. All changes maintain backward compatibility and follow existing codebase patterns.

- **Created** `CacheInvalidationService` for centralized cache management

- **Added** email masking for non-admin users
- **Created** migration `1748800000000-AddUserSearchVector.ts`

author: wcmchenry3-stack
body:
## Summary

Fixes #1881. Part of epic #1879.

Hard's single-roll EV model sees large_straight EV (~33) >> lone upper die EV (~10) and never holds for the bonus even when close to 63 — multi-turn bonus accumulation is invisible to a one-roll lookahead. As a result, Medium was achieving a 10.4% bonus rate while Hard only reached 3.8%, counterintuitively making Medium the stronger bonus player.

**Fix:** in `holdHard` at `rollsUsed=2`, inflate the adjusted EV of mono-face upper-die hold patterns by a proximity tolerance that scales linearly from 0 at `toBonus=30` to 35 pts at `toBonus=0`. The tolerance only applies to same-face holds (e.g. hold all 6s), not to 4-runs or mixed patterns, so straight pursuit is unaffected when the bonus is far away.

THRESHOLD=40 was tested and found to push Hard vs Hard outside [45%,55%] (55.8% — asymmetry from tolerance near the 4-run EV margin). THRESHOLD=30 keeps Hard vs Hard at 51% and is the chosen value.

## Results (n=500)

| Metric | Before | After | Target |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hard bonus rate (vs Hard) | 2.6% | **4.2%** | — |
| Hard bonus rate (vs Medium) | 3.8% | **6.0%** | ≥ 6% ✓ |
| Hard vs Hard win rate | 51.2% | **51.0%** | [45%, 55%] ✓ |
| Hard vs Medium win rate | 55.4% | 53.6% | [58%, 72%] — addressed in #1880 |

Hard vs Medium win rate is within the ±4.4pp CI of baseline (no statistically significant regression). The remaining gap to 58% will be addressed by updating the simulation bands in #1880, which were set before Medium's bonus improvements.

## Test plan

- [x] `jest --testPathPattern="yacht/__tests__/ai\.test"` — 44 tests, all green
- [x] New test: holds upper face over 4-run at `toBonus=20` (EV within threshold)
- [x] New test: still holds 4-run at `toBonus=45` (outside threshold, no override)
- [x] Existing tests: far-from-bonus case (`toBonus=63`) unaffected

author: fred0r
body:
Prevents SIGSEGV when host_client->edict is NULL while dereferencing v.solid at sv_user.cpp:1053. The edict pointer can become NULL during entity callbacks (e.g. pfnCmdStart, pfnPlayerPreThink, pfnPM_Move) when a plugin triggers SV_DropClient within the same frame.

## Purpose

HLDS crashes with SIGSEGV (signal 11) at `engine_i486.so` offset `0x2304b` inside
`SV_RunCmd`. The instruction `mov 0x18c(%ecx),%esi` dereferences `host_client->edict->v.solid`
where `host_client->edict` is NULL. Fault address: `0x18c`.

Trigger: an AMXX plugin (ATAC team-attack counter + AMXBans) calls `SV_DropClient` via
the command buffer during an entity callback that fires inside `SV_RunCmd` before line 1053,
notably `pfnCmdStart`, `pfnPlayerPreThink`, `pfnPlayerThink`, or `pfnPM_Move`. Once
`host_client->edict` is nulled by `SV_DropClient_internal` in `host.cpp:518`, any
subsequent dereference in the same frame crashes.

Reproducible across multiple maps; confirmed in 5+ core dumps and minidumps from
a CS 1.6 server running reHLDS 3.15.0.896 + AMXX 1.10.0.5476.

## Approach

Add a single NULL guard: `if (host_client->edict && host_client->edict->v.solid)`.
When the edict pointer is NULL the entire `SV_LinkEdict` / touch-handling block is
skipped, which is safe because there is no entity to link. The function then proceeds
to `pfnPlayerPostThink` and `pfnCmdEnd`

The fix is minimal — one addition — and does not alter any logic paths for valid entities.

#### Open Questions and Pre-Merge TODOs
- [x] Verified binary disassembly matches source: `0x18c` = `edict->v.solid` (edict offset `0x80` + entvars `solid` at `0x10c`)
- [x] Confirmed 5 independent crash dumps share the same EIP
- [x] Root cause traced to `SV_DropClient` nulling `cl->edict` mid-frame via plugin callbacks
- [X] Backport to upstream reHLDS: the same bug exists in ReHLDS `master` at `sv_user.cpp:1053`

## Learning

The failed `pClient->edict` pointer at offset `0x4a84` in `client_t` was identified by
tracing the crash EIP to the disassembly, cross-referencing with `progdefs.h` (`entvars_t`
layout) and `server.h` (`client_s` layout). The engine misses the NULL check because
vanilla HLDS never exposes `host_client->edict` to callbacks that can drop the client
— this became visible only with AMXX/metamod hooking the entity interface at every
movement callback stage.

`addr2line` confirmed: `SV_RunCmd(usercmd_s*, int, int, int)`.
`eu-readelf -n` on the core dump provided signal, register, and memory-map data.
`objdump -d` provided the exact instruction-level trace.

author: augusto-dmh
body:
## Why

Kappy needs an identity layer before any GitHub App or code-review work can exist. A user signs in with their GitHub identity, and every user needs an **Account** — the ownership and billing boundary that installations, repositories, and reviews will later hang off. This change lands that foundational domain so the GitHub login flow and account-scoped surfaces have models to build on, without yet introducing any authentication flow, authorization policy, or UI.

## What changed

- Introduced an `identity` domain module (`Modules\Identity`) to own the account/membership model, while shared authentication stays in the application core.
- Added an `Account` model with an `AccountType` (Personal / Organization) enum, backed by an `accounts` table keyed to a unique GitHub account id; `type` is cast to the enum.
- Added a `Membership` pivot linking users to accounts with a `MembershipRole` (Owner / Admin / Member), unique per user + account and cascading when a user or account is removed. Accounts expose `members()` and `memberships()`, with the role available as an enum on the pivot.
- Extended `users` with GitHub identity fields (`github_id`, `github_login`, `avatar_url`, `github_token`) and made `password` nullable so GitHub-only accounts can exist. `github_token` is **encrypted at rest** and hidden from serialization; the rollback safely backfills any password-less rows before restoring the constraint.
- Wired the `User` ↔ account relations (`accounts()`, `memberships()`, `personalAccount()`) and updated the user factory.

**Verification:** `vendor/bin/pint --test`, `php artisan test --compact` (49 tests green — new feature tests cover enum casts, the unique-membership constraint, `github_token` encryption-at-rest, the personal-account type filter, and account resolution), plus `npm run lint:check`, `npm run format:check`, `npm run types:check`, and `npm run build` all pass with no regressions to the existing auth/settings/dashboard suite.

author: kennguy3n
body:
## Summary

Closes the 4-hour staleness window on `communication_histories` by publishing a per-message sighting on `es.management.comm_history.update` after every evaluate, and consuming it inline into Postgres. The `relationship_worker` 4h cycle still owns aggregated stats and `typical_hour` recompute; this PR adds an incremental hot path between cycles so the *next* message from the same sender sees an up-to-date row instead of a stale 4-hours-ago snapshot.

**First production writer of `communication_histories`.** No code currently writes the table — the worker only recomputes derived columns. So the partition of ownership matters:

| column | this PR (`RecordSighting`) | worker (`UpdateCountsIfFresh`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `count_7d`, `count_30d` | +1 atomic, `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE` | recompute from snapshots |
| `last_seen_at` | monotonic `GREATEST()` | recompute |
| `sender_domain[_hash]` | one-way backfill iff persisted empty | unchanged |
| `first_seen_at`, `relationship`, `typical_hour` | never touched | owned |

Neither side ever cross-writes the other's columns. The contract on `RecordSighting` is **best-effort monotonic increment, not exactly-once** — JetStream's broker-side dedup window does the heavy lifting, and the worker's 4h cycle recomputes the authoritative state on every pass so any drift self-heals.

## Wire shape

```
evaluate.request
  → handleEvaluateRequest
    → Enrich (read path, hashes (tenant, sender, recipient))
    → Evaluate
    → publishCommHistoryUpdate
        ↓ dedup_id = SHA256-base64url(len-prefixed tenant|sender_hash|recipient_hash|message_id)
        ↓ subject  = es.management.comm_history.update
        ↓ stream   = ES_MANAGEMENT (work-queue, 24h MaxAge, 2m dedup window)
    → publish es.evaluate.result          (existing)
  ↳ handleCommHistoryUpdate (durable: comm-history-update, MaxDeliver=3)
    → CommunicationHistories.RecordSighting
        ↓ Postgres: INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (tid, sender_hash, recipient_hash) DO UPDATE
                    SET count_7d = c.count_7d + 1,
                        count_30d = c.count_30d + 1,
                        last_seen_at = GREATEST(c.last_seen_at, EXCLUDED.last_seen_at),
                        sender_domain = COALESCE(NULLIF(c.sender_domain, ''), EXCLUDED.sender_domain),
                        sender_domain_hash = ... same backfill ...
```

## Key design points

- **Symmetry on the normalisation cascade.** `SightingFor` lives on the same `SignalEnricher` type as `Enrich`. Both apply `TrimSpace` + `ToLower` + PII hasher in the exact same order — without this, the publisher could emit a `(sender_hash, recipient_hash)` pair that never matches the row keys the read path `Get`s, and every message would look like first-contact forever.

  ```go
  // internal/service/evaluate/enricher.go
  type SignalEnricher interface {
      Enrich(ctx, req, base) RiskSignals
      SightingFor(ctx, req) (CommHistoryUpdate, bool) // <- new
  }
  ```

- **Atomic increment.** Postgres path uses a single `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE`. Memory path is mutex-guarded compare-and-write. No read-modify-write window where two concurrent sightings can lose a count.

- **Error semantics.**
  - *Publisher*: swallows every error (bus blip → log + continue). A NAK on the upstream `evaluate.request` would produce a duplicate `evaluate.result` on the next redelivery, which is worse than a 4h-old sighting.
  - *Consumer*: `return nil` on unmarshal / `Validate` failure (drop the poison-pill); `return err` on transient repo failure (JetStream redelivers up to `MaxDeliver=3`, then the worker catches the gap on its 4h cycle).
  - *Subscription registration*: `critErrs` so startup fails loud if the durable cannot attach — silently degrading to the 4h cycle defeats the point of WS-4a.

- **Dedup.** `DedupID()` is a deterministic hash of `len(tenant)|tenant|len(sender_hash)|sender_hash|len(recipient_hash)|recipient_hash|len(message_id)|message_id`. The length prefixes prevent the obvious `"a"+"b" == "ab"+""` collision. Used as the JetStream `Nats-Msg-Id` header so redeliveries within the 2-minute stream dedup window are collapsed at the broker, not at the consumer.

## What this PR is *not*

- Not a removal of the `relationship_worker` 4h cycle — that still recomputes `count_7d`, `typical_hour`, and `relationship` from snapshots. WS-4a is incremental between cycles; the worker is the authoritative recompute.
- Not a behavioural-baseline ML upgrade. `typical_hour`, `relationship`, and `first_seen_at` remain worker-owned and unchanged.
- Not a NoopEnricher removal. The composition root still substitutes `NoopEnricher` when the repo or PII hasher is missing; in that case `SightingFor` returns `(zero, false)` and the publisher short-circuits.

## Test coverage

Local tests pass (`go test ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `golangci-lint run`).

| test | covers |
| --- | --- |
| `TestMemoryCommHistory_RecordSighting_*` (5 cases) | first-contact insert, monotonic last_seen_at, one-way sender_domain backfill, concurrent increment correctness, validation rejection |
| `TestWS4A_EvaluateRequestPublishesCommHistoryUpdate` | producer side: publish on the right subject, exact derived bytes for `sender_hash` / `recipient_hash` / `sender_domain_hash` |
| `TestWS4A_PublishConsumerRoundTripRecordsSighting` | end-to-end via in-process loopback bus: publish → consume → `RecordSighting` lands |
| `TestWS4A_DuplicateMessageIDProducesSameDedupID` | dedup determinism across redeliveries |
| `TestWS4A_ConsumerReturnsErrorOnTransientRepoFailure` | retry contract: surfaces err so JetStream redelivers |
| `TestWS4A_ConsumerReturnsNilOnPoisonMessage` | poison-pill contract: drop on unmarshal / validate failure |
| `TestWS4A_PublisherSkipsWhenSightingForReturnsFalse` | NoopEnricher fallback: no orphaned zero-sightings on the bus |

body:
## Summary

Implements a per-activity circuit breaker that fast-fails activity dispatch when a downstream service is hard-down, preventing retry storms and DLQ floods. When a breaker trips open, new dispatches immediately fail with a non-retryable `CircuitOpen` error instead of burning through the retry policy against a dead target.

## Key Changes

- **New `circuit_breaker.rs` module**: Complete state machine implementation with three phases (Closed → Open → HalfOpen). Tracks failures in a rolling window, trips when threshold is crossed, and admits a single probe after cooldown elapses. State is in-process and per-shard; never touches the event log.

- **`CircuitBreakerPolicy` in `policy.rs`**: New configuration type with `failure_threshold`, `window`, and `cooldown` parameters. Declared via `#[activity(circuit_breaker = ...)]` macro attribute.

- **Activity macro support**: `#[activity]` now accepts optional `circuit_breaker` parameter; macro emits policy into `ActivityInfo::circuit_breaker` field.

- **Worker integration**: `HandlerRegistry` builds `CircuitBreakerRegistry` from declared policies and exposes it via `circuit_breakers()` method. Worker dispatch path consults breaker before executing activities.

- **Management API endpoints** (4 new routes):
  - `GET /admin/circuits` — list all breakers with current state
  - `GET /admin/circuits/{activity_name}` — inspect single breaker
  - `POST /admin/circuits/{activity_name}/force-open` — operator pin (manual incident response)
  - `POST /admin/circuits/{activity_name}/force-close` — operator unpin (resume normal tracking)

- **Failure handling**: New `ActivityFailure::circuit_open()` constructor and `ERROR_TYPE_CIRCUIT_OPEN` constant. Short-circuited attempts record ordinary `ActivityFailed` events with typed `"CircuitOpen"` payload, preserving append-only contract and deterministic replay.

- **Metrics**: Two new counters (`harvest.activity.circuit.tripped`, `harvest.activity.circuit.closed`) emitted on state transitions.

- **Comprehensive tests**: Unit tests in `circuit_breaker.rs`, wiring tests in `circuit_breaker_wiring_tests.rs`, and e2e integration test in `integration_e2e.rs` verifying full dispatch + replay path.

- **Documentation**: Runbook at `docs/runbooks/activity-circuit-breaker.md` with state model, policy declaration examples, workflow error handling patterns, and decision matrix vs. retry/jitter/rate-limit.

## Implementation Details

- State is `Mutex<HashMap<String, BreakerState>>` — in-process, per-shard, never persisted.
- Failure timestamps stored in `VecDeque` for efficient rolling-window pruning.
- `on_dispatch()` performs open → half-open transition when cooldown elapses and admits exactly one probe.
- `on_result()` returns `Option<CircuitTransition>` for metric emission on state changes.
- Operator pins (`forced_open`) override organic state and ignore results until force-closed.
- Activities without a declared policy always return `Allow` and are never tracked.
- Snapshot includes wall-clock trip time, rolling failure count, time-until-probe, and configured thresholds for observability.

## Backward Compatibility

Fully backward compatible. Activities without a declared `CircuitBreakerPolicy` retain today's behavior (no breaker, full retry policy applies). The `circuit_breaker` field on `ActivityInfo` is optional and defaults to `None`.

**💡 What:** We updated `call_center_simulation.py` to stop eagerly creating a boolean list of thread states (`[not fresher.is_alive() for fresher in freshers]`) when assigning incoming calls to freshers. Instead, the raw `freshers` list is passed directly to `find_free_fresher_index`.

**🎯 Why:** The eager evaluation evaluated the `.is_alive()` property of all 1000 fresher threads on every single incoming call, introducing a huge O(N) overhead per call.

**📊 Impact:** Since `find_free_fresher_index` contains a short-circuiting loop that returns upon finding the first available thread, this provides a massive performance boost when many employees are available, bypassing hundreds of thousands of redundant state checks over a simulation run.

💡 What: Removed redundant and pessimistic calls to `reserve_exact` across `scene.rs` and `cpu_renderer.rs`.
🎯 Why: Using `reserve_exact` right before dynamically populated vectors (or before `clone_from`) defeats Rust's standard amortized `O(1)` doubling growth logic. In rendering loops where scene size or command length dynamically increases slightly frame-over-frame, `reserve_exact` forces constant `O(N)` reallocations, creating an `O(N^2)` memory bottleneck. By reverting to `.reserve()` or letting `extend`/`clone_from` naturally handle capacities, we restore optimal container scaling.
📊 Impact: Eliminates O(N) heap reallocation spikes during iterative frame complexity growth by preserving `Vec` doubling.
🔬 Measurement: Run `cargo bench -p abrash-render` or `cargo test -p abrash-render` to ensure correctness without regressions.

body:
## Effect foundation hardening — §10.2/§10.4 bare-op forms + execute the effect suite ×5

A core.effect feasibility probe found the effect surface had gaps hidden behind an **inert** test suite (the `conformance/effects/` fixtures were never checked or executed). This makes the spec §10 bare-op invocation forms work and wires the effect suite into cross-target execution. Three phases.

### Phase B — resolver + checker (`resolve.rs`, `checker.rs`): bare-op resolution per §10.2/§10.3/§10.4
The codegen already established the handler binding and rewrote bare ops against it; only name-injection was missing.
- `resolve_handling` now pushes a scope and injects each handled effect's ops (reusing `inject_ops_for_effect`) before resolving the body → §10.4 bare `log(...)` directly inside `handling { }` resolves (was E1001).
- new `inject_module_handle_operations` injects module-level `handle Effect with X` ops into module scope → §10.3 Layer-2.
- `checker.rs` `HandlingBlock` arm + a module-handle pass mirror the resolver (scoped env injection), so the bare ops type-check.
- Injection stays scoped to handler-in-scope contexts, so a genuinely-unhandled op still errors.

### Phase C — Rust codegen (`rs.rs`): effect op inside string interpolation
The `Interpolation` sub-context now clones `effect_ops`/`current_handler_vars`/`fn_effects`/`composite_effects` → an op inside `${…}` rewrites to its handler call (was rustc E0425, Rust-only). The spec's own §10.2 example (`log(Info, "Started at ${now()}")`) now compiles on Rust. #152-shaped.

### Phase A — harness + fixtures (`execution.rs`, `conformance/`): the effect suite now EXECUTES ×5
- 6 new `exec_effect_*.bock` fixtures, each `// EXPECT: output …` + `targets js, ts, python, rust, go`: `with_clause` (§10.2 incl. op-in-interpolation — the Rust-fix proof), `handling_block` (§10.4), `multiple_effects`, `innermost_handler` (§10.3 shadow), `module_handler` (§10.3 Layer-2), `cross_module`.
- The previously **inert** check-only `effects/` fixtures were **converted** to these executable versions (same scenarios, now run ×5) — `handler_record_impl`/`module_handler_resolves`/`multiple_effects`/`handler_over_with_clause_fn` superseded; `innermost_handler_wins` renamed.
- a check-driven harness test now actually runs `bock check` over the remaining diagnostic fixtures (`lambda_handler_reserved`, `unhandled_effect_error`).

### Verification (independently re-run on the merge candidate; all 5 toolchains present)
fmt ✓ · clippy `--all-targets -D warnings` ✓ · `test --workspace` ✓ (0 failed) · `cargo doc -D warnings` ✓ · `BOCK_CONFORMANCE_REQUIRE=all` → **330 exec passed (incl. all 6 effect fixtures ×5), 0 failed, 0 skipped**. No regression.

### Notes / follow-ups
- **E1001 vs E8020 (residual, by design):** a genuinely-unhandled bare op surfaces resolver `E1001` (undefined name), not the capability-pass `E8020` — `EffectOp` AIR nodes are only built in test code, so E8020 never fires on real bare calls. Kept E1001 for v1 (retargeted `unhandled_effect_error.bock`); unifying them (lowering bare unhandled calls to `EffectOp`) is a separate follow-up (`Q-effect-op-node-lowering`). The diagnostic code is non-normative (§10.3 requires a compile error, which E1001 is).
- **`pure_function.bock` removed:** it asserted `no_errors` for `pure fn` syntax that **does not exist** in the grammar (E2050) and never ran — a speculative/wrong fixture, not a real feature gap (§10.5 pure-effect determinism is `@deterministic`).
- **Minor (cosmetic):** an imported effect referenced only in a `handling (Log with …)` position triggers a `W1001 unused import` — doesn't fail check/exec.

## Summary

Unblocks PR #35 (Dependabot bump of the aspire group). CodeRabbit correctly flagged the alignment issue on #35: Directory.Packages.props bumps \`Aspire.Hosting.*\` to 13.3.5, but \`NextAurora.AppHost.csproj\` is still on \`Aspire.AppHost.Sdk/13.3.0\`. Dependabot can't bump the SDK because it's a \`<Project Sdk=\"...\">\` attribute, not a NuGet PackageVersion — outside its visibility.

This is exactly the CLAUDE.md rule the project encoded:

> \"Aspire SDK and runtime packages must match — including minor versions. The Aspire.AppHost.Sdk/X.Y.Z declared in NextAurora.AppHost.csproj and the Aspire.Hosting.* package versions in Directory.Packages.props need to match exactly (or the SDK ≥ packages).\"

-<Project Sdk=\"Aspire.AppHost.Sdk/13.3.0\">
+<Project Sdk=\"Aspire.AppHost.Sdk/13.3.5\">
\`\`\`

Intermediate state after merge (before #35 rebases): SDK 13.3.5 + packages 13.3.0. The CLAUDE.md rule allows \`SDK ≥ packages\`, so AppHost still boots cleanly. Once #35 rebases against this, both align at 13.3.5 (exact match).

Same shape as PR #33 (EF Core bump that unblocked PR #32's microsoft-extensions group): a small companion PR against main that lifts a floor Dependabot can't see, so the grouped bump can rebase cleanly.
